Alyssa — thanks for the clear list and for joining the call. Recap of where Redwood stands today and concrete asks from you to scope the PoC: 

Summary (short):
- Hosted API: multi-tenant, best for rapid dev/test. Not recommended where data sovereignty/isolation is required.
- Dedicated: single-customer GPU pools, isolated runtime, shared Redwood control plane. Storage and model artifacts sit on tenant-dedicated volumes; we do not mix customer data on the same volumes, but the control plane metadata (e.g., routing, job scheduling) is in Redwood-managed systems.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed control plane option (VPC + peering or on-prem bundle). Full network isolation with customer-controlled ingress/egress. Recommended for regulated PHI/PII workloads.

Direct answers to your bullets: 
- Custody: In Dedicated, customer data is isolated at the block volume level; snapshots are tenant-scoped. There are no co-mingled data volumes for inference data. However, control plane metadata remains in our service unless you opt for Private (VPC/on-prem) where that control plane can be on your side.
- KMS/BYOK: We have integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a BYOK flow (you provide keys and we never persist plaintext). Key rotation and envelope encryption are supported; for Private deployments we can integrate your HSM/KMS directly.
- Network: For Private VPC we support VPC Peering and AWS PrivateLink. For on-prem we provide a connector that establishes mutual TLS and optional routing through a customer gateway — no public egress required.
- Audit logs: We can export comprehensive request logs (request id, timestamp, model, tokens-in/out, requester) to your S3/GCS bucket or a secure syslog. Retention out-of-the-box is 90 days, but for enterprise customers we offer configurable retention up to 24 months (we’ll surface cost implications).

PoC asks / next steps (what we need from MediSys):
1) Confirm target environment: Dedicated or Private VPC (your preference).
2) A short network diagram from Paul showing existing VPCs, NAT/egress, and firewall constraints (helps us scope peering/config).
3) A security questionnaire and one sample dataset (sanitized) we can run through the pipeline for telemetry verification.
4) If BYOK required: an outline of your KMS provider and rotation policy.

I’ve attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level controls), private-vpc-runbook.docx (how we handle peering and connectors), and network-diagram.png (example of a VPC peering layout). Also linking a short runbook so your Ops can review: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b-example-redwood-runbook

Suggested scheduling: technical walkthrough Tue 2026-06-01 10:00am PT with Karthik + Lauren from Redwood and Paul + Alyssa + your Cloud Ops. Does that work?

Cheers,

Hi Alyssa — looping in a few operational details so expectations are clear ahead of the walkthrough: 

Operational commitments (what we can commit in PoC):
- Provisioning: Dedicated pools can be stood up in a sandbox region within 3-5 business days after contract signature. Private VPC setups (peering + IAM integration) typically take 7-14 business days depending on network approvals.
- SLA & monitoring: Dedicated customers get a 99.9% inference runtime SLA option; Private customers can opt for an extended SLA and direct escalation paths into our infra runbook.
- Evidence & compliance: We’ll provide SOC 2 summary artifacts and a curated package for procurement. For deeper audits we can coordinate an on-site/remote interview with our security team if required.

Please note the differences that affect your policy team: Dedicated is operationally faster and less complex for initial rollout, but Private VPC gives the strongest control-plane and egress guarantees which many healthcare customers prefer for PHI.

Next administrative steps:
- Please send us your security questionnaire (or the doc link) and Paul’s preferred contact details for the network diagram upload.
- I’ll open a HubSpot deal RDW-2026-087 and attach the runbook and SOC evidence; Karthik will share the PoC checklist once we confirm the environment.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
